calls.reason: The only usable source, a September FT/Bloomberg report, puts OpenAI's 2026 projection at $36 billion. Whether that counts as 'in the region of' $30 billion is debatable, and no source confirms which projection was current in October.

Reuters' report on the prospectus gives Anthropic obligations that add up to about $413.7 billion, which fits the uncancellable figure. Nothing in the packet reconciles OpenAI's commitments or verifies the combined $1.3 trillion.

His own inputs give a $20.1 billion gap, not $19.1 billion. Anthropic's filing ($16.3B first-half revenue) and its 'crossed $47B' run rate give roughly $18–19 billion. The gist holds roughly, but the exact figure is not supported.

Ramp's 80%/1% figure covers only spending in its own business sample, not each company's total revenue. No evidence shows the top customers are mostly startups or supports the 300–1000% token-spend ratios.

An Apollo figure relayed by Tunguz says 80.4% of top AI spenders are VC-backed. Being VC-backed does not make a firm an AI startup selling subsidized subscriptions, and no breakdown of the customer group was found.

CCIR's table confirms several B300 contracts at about $3.30–$3.98 per hour. The packet does not verify the benchmark rates, could not read the Krea report, and shows no actual payments, so the gaps are not established.
